description: One-factor screen of the ThermoBSP axes on K=3. Seeds 101-180 are disjoint from screen_k3n500 (seeds 1-50). Axis map: T_cav=--cav-temp, T_act=--act-temp, m=--rsb-m, gamma=--rsb-gamma (unfrozen clusters), release=I(k)|DeltaPhi. The CLI --scorer=gamma:<g> is NOT --rsb-gamma.

plot.success_vs_alpha: Primary: which axis moves P(solve). Compare each one-factor cfg to cert.
plot.sigma_note: Run bsp-plot three times with --alpha set to each value above. Slower Sigma descent with flat or higher P(solve) supports the Parisi hypothesis; slower Sigma with worse P(solve) is a false friend.

configs.name: cert
configs.role: BSP 2016 reference: hard SP, certainty scorer, fixed r.

configs.name: dynI
configs.role: Hard free-entropy release via I(k). Measured member of the theory (T=0, m=0).

configs.name: cav_0.05
configs.role: ThermoSP cavity temperature alone; soft warning aggregation, classic backtrack.

configs.name: cav_0.10
configs.role: Stronger cavity temperature; dose check vs cav_0.05.

configs.name: rsb_0.30
configs.role: 1RSB cluster reweighting mu ~ exp(m N s_C); mild m.

configs.name: rsb_0.50
configs.role: Stronger m; expect possible harm if uniform clusters (m=0) were the good regime.

configs.name: act_fth
configs.role: Gibbs action temperature on direction + free-energy scorer; release still uses r.

configs.name: fe_bt
configs.role: Soft release on DeltaPhi and Gibbs back/dec split (r ignored). Needs cav-temp.

configs.name: dynI_cav
configs.role: Interaction: best hard release plus mild ThermoSP messages.

configs.name: soft_rsb
configs.role: Soft package plus mild 1RSB reweighting: tests whether m helps once messages and release are already soft.

configs.name: gamma_0.5
configs.role: Unfrozen-cluster bias at T=0, m=0. Boosts the hard free sector of each cavity star.

configs.name: gamma_1.0
configs.role: Stronger unfrozen bias; dose check vs gamma_0.5.

decision_rules: Promote an axis only if P(solve) beats cert on at least two contiguous alphas with non-overlapping binomial SE, or mean Sigma descent improves without lowering P(solve).
If dynI wins and fe_bt / soft_rsb do not, the hard I(k) corner is the publishable claim; soft temperatures are not helping at this N.
If rsb_* loses to cert, do not raise m in follow-ups; keep m=0.
If cav_* alone helps, T_cav is worth a finer grid; if only dynI_cav helps, the gain is still the release rule.
If soft_rsb beats fe_bt, m helps only inside the soft package; if it loses, stacking m hurts.
If gamma_* loses to cert, do not raise the unfrozen bias; keep gamma=0.
